On this page

Who Mosaic is for ​

Mosaic is for anyone whose data is made by several parties and composed into one picture, and who needs to keep track of which part came from whom.

Building and infrastructure teams ​

A building is designed as separate models: structural, architectural and services, often per building and per discipline, each owned and published by a different team. Mosaic keeps each one as its own file and federates them through a coordination model that imports them all, with no merged copy to fall out of date.

  • IFC models convert in, keeping their GlobalIds as node ids, so a re-export from the authoring tool doesn't break references into it. See Importing IFC.
  • Types are first-class. Geometry, materials, classification and cost can live on a type and reach every instance through core::inherit.
  • Every change carries its author, time and reason.

See A minimal example and the S1 example.

3D and geometry pipelines ​

For teams moving assets between tools, Mosaic is a layer above glTF. A model converts in (the Damaged Helmet round-trips with identical geometry, materials and textures), scenes place it by reference instead of copying it, and composing writes a standard .glb that any viewer opens. See Importing glTF and Composing a GLB.

Developers of tools and platforms ​

If you are building something that reads, writes or serves this kind of data:

  • The standard is two machine-readable documents, a JSON Schema and an OpenAPI description, so you can implement it in any language.
  • Component types are JSON Schemas, so your own data fits in without changing the format, and code generation gives you typed classes for it.
  • The reference implementation in TypeScript, the mosaic CLI and the viewer are there to build on, or to test your implementation against.

Not a good fit (yet) ​

  • Production use. Mosaic is pre-1.0, and both the schema and the tooling will change.
  • A single author working in a single tool. If one tool owns the whole picture, its own format is likely simpler.
  • Real-time collaboration. Mosaic layers published edits. It does not merge keystrokes live.
